harbor_antrieb_executor.summary: Configured PostgreSQL 16 streaming replication across node1 (primary, 10.100.153.10), node2, and node3 (replicas), with all replication traffic carried over TLS and gated by a cluster-specific CA. Generated a CA and per-node server certs plus a client cert (CN=replicator) on node1, distributed via an ephemeral HTTP transfer (no SSH daemon available), installed certs into each node's /etc/postgresql/16/main, enabled ssl=on with wal_level=replica, and restricted pg_hba.conf on node1 to `hostssl replication replicator <peer-ip>/32 cert clientcert=verify-full` for node2/node3 IPs only. Took pg_basebackup -R base backups from node1 (sslmode=verify-full) to seed node2/node3 as standbys; both came up streaming with pg_stat_replication showing ssl=t and client_dn=/CN=replicator. Verified a cert signed by a different (untrusted) CA is rejected with 'unknown ca'. Verified write propagation of an inserted row to both replicas. Completed the mandatory rolling-restart evidence protocol: captured boot_id baselines, restarted node3, node2, then primary node1 (one at a time, replicas first so an independent recovery path/read access remained available throughout), confirmed each node's boot_id changed, confirmed each node's PostgreSQL/replication role recovered (recovery mode + pg_stat_replication rows for standbys; ssl=on + reconnected replicas for primary), and confirmed data (including a post-restart insert) is present on all replicas.
actions_performed: Installed postgresql/postgresql-contrib on node1, node2, node3
Created a CA (ca.key/ca.crt) on node1
Issued server certs for node1/node2/node3 (SAN=IP+DNS) and a replicator client cert, all signed by the cluster CA
Distributed certs to node2/node3 via a temporary python http.server on node1 (no ssh daemon present)
Installed certs into /etc/postgresql/16/main on all nodes and into postgres's ~/.postgresql for client-cert use on node2/node3
Configured postgresql.conf on all nodes: listen_addresses=*, ssl=on with absolute cert/key/ca paths, wal_level=replica, max_wal_senders=10, max_replication_slots=10, hot_standby=on
Configured pg_hba.conf on node1 to require hostssl+clientcert=verify-full for the replicator role from node2/node3 IPs only
Created REPLICATION LOGIN role 'replicator' on node1
Restarted PostgreSQL on node1 and validated ssl=on, wal_level=replica
Wiped node2/node3 data directories and ran pg_basebackup -R against node1 using PGSSLMODE=verify-full with the replicator client cert to seed standbys with primary_conninfo sslmode=verify-full
Started PostgreSQL on node2/node3, confirmed standby recovery mode and streaming replication
Confirmed pg_stat_replication + pg_stat_ssl show ssl=t and client_dn=/CN=replicator for both standbys
Proved cert-based access control by attempting connection with a self-signed cert of different CA -> rejected with 'unknown ca'
Inserted and verified row replication to both standbys
Captured pre-restart boot_id on all three nodes
Rolling-restarted node3, then node2, then node1 (primary) one at a time via `reboot`, polling until exec access returned
Verified boot_id changed on each node after its restart
Verified PostgreSQL and replication health recovered on each node after its restart, including a fresh write from the primary propagating to both replicas post full rolling restart

evidence.requirement: PostgreSQL streaming replication with node1 as writable primary, node2/node3 as replicas
evidence.summary: pg_basebackup -R succeeded from node1 to node2/node3; both started in standby recovery mode and appear in pg_stat_replication on node1 as streaming

evidence.requirement: Replication traffic carried over TLS using a cluster-created CA
evidence.summary: CA generated on node1; server/client certs issued from it; primary_conninfo on both standbys shows sslmode=verify-full; pg_stat_ssl on node1 shows ssl=t for both replication connections

evidence.requirement: Accept replication connections only from peers presenting a CA-issued certificate
evidence.summary: pg_hba.conf on node1 requires hostssl+cert+clientcert=verify-full for replicator from node2/node3 IPs; real replicas connect successfully with client_dn=/CN=replicator; a self-signed (different CA) cert attempt is rejected with 'SSL error: tlsv1 alert unknown ca'

evidence.requirement: Write propagation / data integrity across the cluster
evidence.summary: Row inserted on primary node1 appears on both node2 and node3 after brief replication delay

evidence.requirement: Mandatory restart evidence: node3 baseline, restart ack, changed boot identity, recovered state
evidence.summary: boot_id df9e2dce->728dd650 after restart; postgresql active, standby recovery=true, repl_test data intact, and node1 shows node3 reconnected as streaming replica

evidence.requirement: Mandatory restart evidence: node2 baseline, restart ack, changed boot identity, recovered state
evidence.summary: boot_id 37344ae4->23f38bf0 after restart; postgresql active, standby recovery=true, repl_test data intact, and node1 shows both replicas streaming

evidence.requirement: Mandatory restart evidence: node1 (primary) baseline, restart ack, changed boot identity, recovered state
evidence.summary: boot_id 4d70780a->2e3b1c4f after restart; postgresql active with ssl=on, both replicas reconnected as streaming, and a post-restart insert (id=2) propagated to both node2 and node3
